instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Supportive Rage
cards.instruction: Remain helpful and encouraging while becoming increasingly furious.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've spilled paint on my sofa, but we'll fix it. You're rubbing with a cloth, so I'll do this end the same way.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm blotting, not rubbing. You're spreading it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, blotting. Keep doing that; you're doing well. That was my favourite cushion, damn it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We need another cloth. Mine's full of paint.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take my clean shirt. Another perfectly good thing ruined. Keep going, you're getting it up; I'll hold the cushion for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Six covers, you said, so I've bought six tablecloths. Cost a fortune, but your birthday table will look wonderful.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A cover means a diner. We only need one cloth.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One, yes. The others are spares. Five bloody spares. Choose the nicest; you deserve it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The restaurant supplies the cloth. We can't use any of these.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course they do. Six bloody tablecloths going home untouched. Give me the bag; you go in and choose your seat. You're having a lovely dinner if it kills me.

cards.title: Terms and Conditions
cards.instruction: Treat every offer, favor, feeling, and apology as a negotiation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mate's rates, as you say. Two lifts instead of one for borrowing my ladder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mate's rates means less, not more. I only need it five minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Less cash, yes. One lift, then, and tell your wife my roses have improved.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't you lend it because we're friends?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Say that to your wife too and we can drop the lift. I'll take a public endorsement of the friendship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Clean slate, yes. I've wiped next month's calendar. When will you visit to make up for missing my birthday?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Clean slate means forgiving me, not clearing dates for repayment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Forgiving, exactly. There's room for a whole weekend now. Two nights and I'll stop mentioning it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can come one evening. I'd like you to be happy to see me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One evening with dinner here, then. Bring dessert and I'll be delighted; wash up and I'll mean it right through breakfast.

cards.title: Yes, but My Way
cards.instruction: Agree with others, then reinterpret the agreement entirely in your favor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take an end, yes. I've got the corner of this cushion. I'll help you move the sofa.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cushions are sewn on. Take an end of the sofa itself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely, the whole sofa. You get underneath; I'll take the end of the room and tell you when you're clear.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need a second person lifting, not watching.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. I'll book someone on your phone. You two lift, and I'll give both of you the same countdown.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Heel, yes. I've taken my shoes off so he can see mine. I'll help train your dog.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Heel means walk at your side. He doesn't need to see your feet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely, at your side. You walk him and I'll say heel, just as you did.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You need to be holding the lead if you're training him.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. I'll hold the handle while you hold it near his collar. You choose the route; I'll follow.

cards.title: The Pattern
cards.instruction: Treat every minor detail as evidence of a much larger problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've chalked the doorframe, so I've marked every scratch. Someone's been testing our entrances.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was marking how tall our grandson is.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Precisely, gathering measurements. They know how big he is now. Who can see those marks?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only us. They're inside the house.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then whoever's doing it already has a key. Give me the chalk; we should mark which doors each of our keys opens.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put a red flag on your email, so I've flagged all mine. The whole office must be in trouble.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It means follow up later. Mine's a reminder to order biscuits.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, follow up. If we need warnings to get biscuits ordered, what else is being forgotten?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll remove the flags from the messages you've already answered.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then those won't look urgent at all. Before you erase the warnings, show me how we'll know who's keeping the office supplied.

cards.title: Could You Just…
cards.instruction: Turn a difficult task into tiny favors until the help quietly becomes most of the task.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've tapped these screws with the hammer, like you did. Could you hold the shelf bracket while I finish?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was tapping in wall plugs. Screws turn.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, turn. Could you give the top one a turn while you've got the bracket steady?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's holding now. The other screws are lined up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just turn those too, then slide the shelf on to check it? I'll take the hammer out of your way.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've folded that ribbon back on itself, so I've folded mine. Could you hold it against my wedding bouquet?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was making a bow. You need to wrap the stems first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, the wrapping first. Could you wind it round once while you're holding the stems?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Once won't hold them. I'll wrap the whole handle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Could you finish with that bow of yours? Just tuck the end underneath and pull it tight; I'll hold the scissors.
